staffExcelUpload.title: Staff Excel Upload
staffExcelUpload.subtitle: Upload a staff Excel file for backend processing.
staffExcelUpload.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Staff Excel Upload lets you bulk-import or update staff data by uploading a formatted Excel spreadsheet. The file is transmitted to the processing system and applied automatically. Use this function when onboarding a large number of staff or making bulk updates.

⚠ WARNING — WRONG FORMAT CAN CAUSE DATA PROBLEMS
Uploading an incorrectly formatted file may create corrupt records, overwrite valid data, or trigger processing errors that are difficult to reverse. Always verify your file against the required template before uploading. Do not upload a file you are unsure about.

FILE REQUIREMENTS
• Accepted formats: .xls or .xlsx only. Other file types are rejected immediately.
• The spreadsheet must follow the exact column layout defined in the official staff upload template.
• Column headers must match exactly — do not rename, reorder, or remove columns.
• Do not include blank rows in the middle of the data.
• Ensure all required fields are populated for every row.

HOW TO UPLOAD
1. Prepare your Excel file using the official staff upload template.
2. Double-check all data and column headers before proceeding.
3. Click Select File and choose your .xls or .xlsx file.
4. The selected filename is shown next to the button — confirm it is the correct file.
5. Click Upload. Do not close the page while the upload is in progress.
6. A success message confirms the file was received and processed.
7. If an error message appears, check the file format and try again.

AFTER UPLOADING
• Verify the imported staff records in the Staff list to confirm data is correct.
• If incorrect data was imported, contact your system administrator immediately to arrange a correction.

projectPlanning.title: Project Workbench
projectPlanning.subtitle: Plan and schedule project activities
projectPlanning.helpBody: Plan and schedule project tasks and resources.
projectPlanning.helpIntro: Use Project Workbench to plan streams and tasks, manage resource workspaces, and review schedule progress in Day, Week, and Month views.
projectPlanning.helpAtAGlanceBody: The top summary shows the project code, project name, customer, project dates, and current project status. The toolbar below it gives you the main navigation actions: Add Stream, Inventory Overview, Skill Overview, Manpower Overview, and the Day/Week/Month timeline switch. The left side of the timeline lists each stream and task, while the right side shows the schedule bars or milestone markers.
projectPlanning.helpNavigationBody: Use Back to return to the previous project page. The workbench layout is split into a fixed left panel and a scrollable timeline. The left panel contains row names, dates, settings, and action icons. The timeline on the right can be scrolled horizontally to inspect later periods without losing the row context.
projectPlanning.helpWorkflowBody: A practical working sequence is: 1. create the project streams, 2. add tasks under each stream, 3. assign the person in charge and task dates, 4. open the planning workspaces to add inventory, skills, or manpower, 5. review the Gantt bars for date conflicts, and 6. update task status from the bar when execution starts or finishes.
projectPlanning.helpTimelineBody: Switch between Day, Week, and Month to change the level of detail. Day view is best for short-term checking, Week view for coordination, and Month view for broader planning. Milestone tasks render as diamonds, while normal tasks render as bars. The current day, week, or month is highlighted automatically to help you orient yourself.
projectPlanning.helpCurrentPeriodBody: The current period is highlighted automatically: today in Day view, the current week in Week view, and the current month in Month view. The same highlight is used in the Gantt timeline, Inventory Overview, Skill Overview, and Manpower Overview so you can compare all workstreams against the same time reference.
projectPlanning.helpActionsBody: Each stream or task row has a settings icon and, when applicable, planning icons. Use the settings menu to create child items, edit details, replicate streams, hide or show tasks, link milestone tasks, move tasks to a different parent, or remove items when the rules allow it.
projectPlanning.helpTaskBarStatusBody: Only task bars with status Not Started or In Progress are clickable for status updates. Clicking the bar opens a status dialog with the next allowed status and a date field. Confirm the change, then review the acknowledgement prompt before saving. Not Started changes to In Progress and records the actual start date. In Progress changes to Completed and records the actual end date. Completed tasks are read-only from the bar.
projectPlanning.helpStreamActionsBody: From a stream row you can create a new task, edit the stream information, replicate the entire stream by entering a new stream name, hide or show the stream's tasks, and remove the stream when no tasks remain underneath it. The remove action is disabled if the stream still contains tasks.
projectPlanning.helpTaskActionsBody: From a task row you can create a child task, edit task information, link or remove a milestone task, move the task to another parent, and remove the current task when its type and dependency rules permit. The settings menu shows only the actions that are valid for the selected task.
projectPlanning.helpDependenciesBody: Hover the task-type icon to highlight the parent task and any linked tasks. Hover the task name to inspect task details. The highlight is purely visual and does not change the saved data.
projectPlanning.helpRulesBody: Task type, duration limits, start-date editability, and delete permissions are controlled by task-type settings. Some task types can only be created from a stream, some can only be created from another task, milestone tasks require milestone linking, and tasks with dependent children cannot be deleted until those dependencies are removed.
projectPlanning.helpPlanningWorkspacesBody: Inventory Planning opens a separate workspace for the selected row so you can add stock, asset, or bundle requirements. Stock planning is available on tasks, asset planning is available on streams, and bundle planning is available on both. Skill Workspace is task-based and lets you assign the skills and units required for execution. Manpower Workspace is task-based and lets you assign staff and daily loading. In manpower, past work dates are displayed but the Save button is hidden.
projectPlanning.helpOverviewsBody: Inventory Overview summarizes planned quantities by period and shows the activity name and quantity details on hover. Skill Overview aggregates required units by skill across each period. Manpower Overview shows staff loading by day and highlights overloads in red when total loading exceeds 1.0 for a day.
projectPlanning.helpHowReplicateStreamBody: 1. Open the settings menu on the stream row. 2. Click Replicate Stream. 3. Enter a new stream name in the dialog. 4. Save to create a copy of the stream structure and its tasks.
projectPlanning.helpSectionHowManageTasks: How To: Create And Manage Tasks
projectPlanning.helpHowManageTasksBody: 1. Open the stream settings menu and click Create Task, or open an existing task and click Create Child Task. 2. Fill in the task name, task type, start date, duration, and person in charge. 3. Save the task. 4. Use the task settings menu later to edit, link a milestone, move the task, or remove it when allowed. 5. Use the timeline bar to track execution status after the task starts.
projectPlanning.helpHowMoveTaskBody: 1. Open task settings and click Move To. 2. Move mode activates and the workbench shows valid targets. 3. Click a valid target parent task in the grid. 4. The system recalculates the hierarchy and updates the task placement.
projectPlanning.helpHowInventoryPlanningBody: 1. Click the inventory icon on the relevant row. 2. Choose the Stock, Asset, or Bundle tab. 3. Select a product and enter the required quantity. 4. Add the item, review the list, and remove or adjust entries before closing. 5. Duplicate products are blocked so the same item is not planned twice in the same workspace.
projectPlanning.helpHowManpowerPlanningBody: 1. Click the skill icon on a task row. 2. Select the required skill or skills. 3. Set the unit values and save the selection. 4. If manpower has already been manually updated for the task, the skill requirements are locked and only read-only review is available.
projectPlanning.helpHowReadOverviewsBody: 1. Open Inventory Overview, Skill Overview, or Manpower Overview from the header buttons. 2. Switch Day, Week, or Month to change the granularity. 3. Use the highlighted current period column as the reference point. 4. Hover populated cells to view the detailed breakdown for that activity, skill, or staff member.

userLoginList.title: Login Enquiry
userLoginList.subtitle: View and filter user login activities
userLoginList.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Login Enquiry is a read-only audit log of every user login event recorded by the system. Use it to review when users logged in, which login method they used, and to investigate suspicious or unusual access.

KEY CONCEPTS
• Login Time — the exact date and time the login event occurred, shown in your local timezone.
• Login Type — the method used to log in (e.g. password, token, SSO).
• User — the account that performed the login.

ACCESS CONTROL
• You can only see login records for users in your own company whose level does not exceed your own.
• Records are sorted newest first by default.

FILTERING THE RESULTS
Four independent filters are available and can be combined freely:
• Search — type any part of a user's name or login type to instantly filter results.
• User dropdown — select a specific user to see only their login events.
• Start Date — show only records on or after this date.
• End Date — show only records on or before this date (inclusive up to 23:59:59).
Click Clear to reset all filters and show the full list.

uomHierarchy.title: Product Hierarchy
uomHierarchy.subtitle: Define product packaging relationships — e.g. how many units make up a box
uomHierarchy.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Product Hierarchy defines how products are packaged or aggregated. For example, 1 Box contains 12 Bottles, or 1 Pallet contains 10 Boxes. These relationships are used to convert between units of measure when issuing or receiving stock.

KEY CONCEPTS
• Parent product — the container or larger unit (e.g. Box, Carton, Pallet).
• Child product — the component or smaller unit stored inside the parent (e.g. Bottle, Piece, Unit).
• Child quantity per parent — how many child units make up exactly one parent unit (must be 2 or more).

RULES
• A product cannot be its own parent or child.
• Each product can only appear in one hierarchy relationship at a time (either as a parent or as a child). A product already assigned to a relationship is excluded from the selection lists.
• Child quantity must be greater than 1.

HOW TO ADD A PRODUCT HIERARCHY
1. Click 'Add Hierarchy'.
2. Select the Parent Product from the dropdown. Only products not already in a relationship are shown.
3. Select the Child Product. The parent product is automatically excluded from this list.
4. Enter the Child Quantity per Parent (minimum 2).
5. Click Save.

HOW TO EDIT A PRODUCT HIERARCHY
1. Click the edit icon on the row you want to change.
2. Adjust the parent, child, or quantity as needed.
3. Click Save. Only products used in other relationships are excluded — the current record's own products remain selectable.

HOW TO DELETE A PRODUCT HIERARCHY
1. Click the delete icon on the row.
2. A confirmation dialog shows the relationship details.
3. Click Confirm to permanently remove the hierarchy definition.

SEARCHING
Use the search bar at the top to filter by parent product name/code or child product name/code. Results update as you type.

productBundle.title: Product Bundles
productBundle.subtitle: Group products that serve the same purpose into bundles
productBundle.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Product Bundle lets you group products that serve the same purpose so they can be treated as a set. For example, a spare parts kit or a set of tools that are always issued together. Each bundle has a unique code, a name, and at least two member products.

RULES
• Bundle Code and Bundle Name are both mandatory.
• A bundle must have at least 2 member products.
• Each product can only belong to one bundle at a time. Products already in another bundle are excluded from the selection list.
• Products that share a parent/child relationship in the Product Hierarchy cannot be placed in the same bundle (e.g. if "Box" is the parent of "Unit", they cannot both be bundle members).

HOW TO ADD A BUNDLE
1. Click Add Bundle.
2. Enter a Bundle Code (unique identifier).
3. Enter a Bundle Name (descriptive label).
4. In the Bundle Members field, type to search and select at least 2 products. Products already bundled or linked via hierarchy to a selected member are automatically excluded.
5. Click Save.

OVERVIEW
User Management allows administrators to create, view, edit, and deactivate system user accounts. Each user belongs to a company and is assigned a level that controls what they can see and do within the system.

KEY CONCEPTS
• Login — the unique username a user enters to sign in. Must be unique across the system.
• Level — a numeric access tier. A user can only manage (create or view) users at or below their own level. Lower numbers are more restricted; higher numbers have broader access.
• Company — the organisation the user belongs to. Users without the BaseSetup role can only see users in their own company.
• Active — when inactive, the user cannot log in. Use this instead of deletion to temporarily suspend access.
• PW Last Changed — the date the user last changed their password, shown for audit purposes.

ACCESS CONTROL
• Administrators can manage users across all companies and all levels.
• Regular users can only see users from their own company, and only users whose level is equal to or lower than their own.
• The Level field when adding a user is capped at the current user's own level.

HOW TO ADD A USER
1. Click Add User.
2. Enter the user's First Name and Last Name (both required).
3. Enter a unique Login name (required).
4. Enter a Password (required). The user should change this after first login.
5. Optionally enter a Mobile Number.
6. Select a Level (0 is the lowest; options are capped at your own level).
7. Select the Company the user belongs to.
8. Check or uncheck Active as appropriate (defaults to active).
9. Click Save.

HOW TO EDIT A USER
1. Click the edit icon on the user's row.
2. Modify any field as needed.
3. Leave the password field blank to keep the existing password, or enter a new one to change it.
4. Click Save.

HOW TO DELETE A USER
1. Click the delete icon on the user's row.
2. A confirmation screen shows the user's details.
3. Click Confirm to permanently remove the user.

forcedPassword.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Forced Password allows an authorized administrator to set a new password for another user account. This is useful for account recovery or security resets when a user cannot change their own password.

ACCESS CONTROL
• You can only target users whose level is less than or equal to your own level.
• If you do not have cross-company permission, only users in your own company are available.
• Your own account cannot be selected as the target user.

REQUIRED FIELDS
• Target User — the account whose password will be replaced.
• New Password — the password to set for the target user (minimum 8 characters).
• Confirm New Password — must exactly match New Password.
• Your Current Password — used to verify your authority before request submission.

HOW TO FORCE CHANGE A PASSWORD
1. Select a target user from the dropdown list.
2. Enter the new password and confirm it.
3. Enter your current password.
4. Click Force Password Change.
5. Wait for the success message before leaving the page.

ERROR HANDLING
• Invalid password means your current password verification failed.
• Requesting user not found or inactive means your account state is invalid for this action.
• Target user not found means the selected user is no longer valid.
• Network or server errors should be retried after checking connectivity or backend health.

purchaseOrderList.subtitle: Manage purchase orders
purchaseOrderList.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Purchase Orders record goods or services ordered from a vendor. Each order has a header with vendor, date, and status, plus one or more line items specifying what was ordered, in what quantity, and at what price.

ORDER STATUS
• New — the order has been created but not yet acted upon.
• Processing — the order is being fulfilled or awaiting delivery.
• Completed — all items have been received and the order is closed.
• Cancelled — the order was cancelled and will not be fulfilled.

FIELDS — ORDER HEADER
• Order ID — a unique identifier for the order. The system automatically prefixes it with your company ID.
• Vendor — the supplier for this order. Required.
• Order Date — the date the order was placed. Defaults to today.
• Order Status — current state of the order.

FIELDS — LINE ITEMS
• Product Code — the vendor's product code for the ordered item. Required.
• Item Type — Inventory (I) for stock items; Assets (A) for fixed-asset purchases.
• Internal Product Code — your company's internal code for the product.
• Internal Order ID — an internal reference number if required.
• Quantity — number of units ordered. Must be greater than 0.
• Unit Price — price per unit. Must be 0 or greater.
• Line Total — calculated automatically (Quantity × Unit Price).
• Total — sum of all line totals, shown at the bottom of the items table.

HOW TO ADD A PURCHASE ORDER
1. Click Add.
2. Enter a unique Order ID.
3. Select a Vendor (required).
4. Set the Order Date (defaults to today).
5. Set the Order Status as appropriate.
6. Click Add Item to add at least one line item.
7. For each item: enter the Product Code, select Item Type, optionally fill Internal Product Code and Internal Order ID, then set Quantity and Unit Price.
8. Repeat steps 6–7 for additional items. Remove any unwanted item with the delete icon on its row.
9. Click Save. The order cannot be saved without at least one valid line item.

HOW TO VIEW A PURCHASE ORDER
Click the view (eye) icon on the order's row to open a read-only detail screen showing the order header and all line items.

HOW TO EDIT A PURCHASE ORDER
1. Click the edit icon on the order's row.
2. Modify the header fields or line items as needed.
3. Add new items or remove existing ones using the item row controls.
4. Click Save.

HOW TO DELETE A PURCHASE ORDER
1. Click the delete icon on the order's row.
2. A warning confirms that all associated line items will also be deleted and the action cannot be undone.
3. Click Confirm to permanently delete the order.

SEARCHING
Use the search bar to filter by order ID, vendor name, or order status. Results update as you type.

staffProfile.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
The Staff Profile section is the central hub for managing and analysing staff competency data. It brings together four views — Staff Skill Profile, Staff Merit Profile, Staff Skill Analysis, and Staff Merit Analysis — all accessible from the dashboard.

Administrators (user level 9) can see all staff across all companies. Other users see only the staff belonging to their own company.

DASHBOARD
The dashboard opens by default and displays four summary cards:
• Total Staff — number of staff members currently in scope.
• Skill Sets — number of distinct skill sets recorded.
• Overall Merit — aggregate merit score across all staff.
• Overall Demerit — aggregate demerit score across all staff.

Use the action buttons on the dashboard to navigate to each sub-view.

STAFF SKILL PROFILE
Manage the skills assigned to individual staff members.

Viewing a staff member's skills:
1. Click Staff Skill Profile on the dashboard.
2. The staff list is displayed. Use the search bar to filter by name, ID, or other details.
3. Click a staff member to open their personal skill profile, showing all assigned skills with skill name, category, description, issuer, acquired date, and expiry date.

Adding a skill to a staff member:
1. Open the staff member's skill profile.
2. Click Add Skill.
3. Browse or search the skill catalogue. Filter by category if needed.
4. Select a skill from the list.
5. Fill in the skill assignment details:
   • Issued By — the issuing authority or trainer.
   • Acquired Date — when the staff member obtained the skill.
   • Expiry Date — when the certification expires (if applicable).
   • No Expiry — tick this if the skill does not expire; overrides the Expiry Date field.
   • Certification — upload supporting documents or certificates via the gallery.
6. Click Save.

Note: If a skill does not exist in the catalogue yet, you can create it directly from the Add Skill screen by entering a Skill Name, Description, and Category.

Editing a skill assignment:
1. In the staff member's skill profile, click the edit (pencil) icon on the skill row.
2. Modify the Issued By, Acquired Date, Expiry Date, No Expiry, or Certification as needed.
3. Click Save.

Deleting a skill assignment:
1. Click the delete icon on the skill row.
2. Confirm the deletion. Only the assignment is removed from that staff member's profile; the skill itself remains in the catalogue.

Navigating back:
• Click Back to return from a staff member's skill profile to the staff list.
• Click Back again to return to the main dashboard.

STAFF MERIT PROFILE
View and manage merit and demerit records for each staff member. (This view is under active development.)

STAFF SKILL ANALYSIS
View cross-staff skill coverage and gap analysis charts and reports. (This view is under active development.)

STAFF MERIT ANALYSIS
View cross-staff merit and demerit trend analysis. (This view is under active development.)

staffManagement.projectSkillMatchSubtitle: Compare project skill requirements with currently valid staff skills.
staffManagement.projectSkillMatchHelpBody:
The report counts by skill and by day, not as one total across all tasks.

If the same skill appears in multiple tasks on the same day, the required units are first aggregated for that skill. Matching then compares the aggregated requirement with the number of unique qualified staff available for that skill.

Example 1: Task 1 needs Skill A (2 units) and Task 2 needs Skill A (1 unit). Three staff have Skill A. Result: required 3, matched 3, shortage 0, excess 0.

Example 2: Task 1 needs Skill A (2 units) and Task 2 needs Skill A (1 unit). Two staff have Skill A. Result: required 3, matched 2, shortage 1, excess 0.

Example 3: Task 1 needs Skill A (2 units) and Task 2 needs Skill A (1 unit). Four staff have Skill A. Result: required 3, matched 3, shortage 0, excess 1.

Example 4: Staff 1 has Skill A and Skill B. Task 1 needs Skill A. Task 2 needs Skill B. Staff 1 can satisfy both skills separately because the report counts each skill requirement independently.

stockAdjustment.title: Stock Adjustment
stockAdjustment.subtitle: Scan or enter stock code and record stock adjustments
stockAdjustment.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock Adjustment is used to correct stock quantities when the physical count differs from the system record. Two types are available: In Adjustment (increases the stock balance) and Out Adjustment (decreases the stock balance). Each adjustment requires a reference and records a movement in the system.

HOW TO RECORD A STOCK ADJUSTMENT

Step 1 — Scan or enter the stock code
Type the stock code in the input field, or tap the QR/barcode scanner icon to open the camera and scan a barcode or QR code. Then click Find Stock.
You may also click the search icon to look up a stock code by product name or code.

Step 2 — Review the stock locations
If the stock code is found, the product name is displayed along with a table of stock lines showing each storage location, its current quantity, and available quantity. If the code is not found, a warning is shown — verify the code and try again.

Step 3 — Select a location
Click the row for the storage location you want to adjust. The row is highlighted and a tick appears in the Select column.

Step 4 — Choose the adjustment type
Use the toggle buttons to select:
• In Adjustment — adds to the stock balance (e.g., stock found during a count)
• Out Adjustment — reduces the stock balance (e.g., stock written off or found short)

Step 5 — Enter the reference
Type a reference in the Reference field (e.g., an audit number, reason code, or document number). This explains the reason for the adjustment. Your name is automatically appended to the reference when the record is saved.

Step 6 — Enter the adjustment quantity
Enter the quantity to adjust in the Adjustment field. Must be greater than zero. The unit of measure is shown next to the field.

Step 7 — Click Save
The adjustment movement is saved, an Adjustment Note PDF is generated and stored in the document library, and the stock table refreshes to show updated quantities. A success message is displayed. The Adjustment field resets to 1 and the Reason/Reference fields clear, ready for the next entry.

QR / BARCODE SCANNER
• Tap the scanner icon inside the stock code field to open the camera scanner.
• Point the camera at a QR code or barcode — it is decoded automatically and the search runs without needing to press Find Stock.
• The scanner closes automatically after a successful scan.
• Camera access must be permitted in your browser settings.

stockTakeOn.title: Stock Take On
stockTakeOn.subtitle: Scan or enter stock code and record take-on quantities
stockTakeOn.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock Take On records opening stock (movement type N) when items are first introduced into the system. The process supports stock-code scanning, product matching/linking, optional product creation, location selection, and quantity recording.

UPDATED FLOW
1. Scan or enter stock code
Type the stock code or use the scanner icon in the stock-code field. After scan/input, run stock lookup.

2. If stock is found
The product and stock rows are displayed.
• Select a stock row/location.
• If needed, choose another existing location or create a new location (only when location limit allows).

3. If stock is NOT found
A product matching dialog with a list of products opens.
• User can select product from the product list to link a new stock code to a product.
• Optionally click on AI Product Search button to let AI find out what product the stock code is.
• Review candidate products and select one, then click Use Selected Product to link the stock code.
• If none is suitable, click No Product Matches to open Create New Product.

AI PRODUCT SEARCH (IMPORTANT)
• AI returns candidate products and may provide a suggested name/description for prefill.
• AI does NOT create products and does NOT auto-link stock codes.
• Linking happens only when you explicitly click Use Selected Product, or when you save a newly created product.
• If AI matching is unavailable, you can still choose an existing product manually or create a new product.

4. Create New Product path
In Create New Product, fill required fields (Product Code, Product Name, Category, UOM, and at least one image).
• Save Product And Continue: creates product, links stock code, and returns to take-on flow.
• Back to Product Selection: returns to candidate list without creating product.

5. Enter quantity and location
Enter Take On Quantity (> 0), confirm selected location, then submit Record Quantity.

6. Confirm result
A success message appears and latest record summary is shown for verification. Form resets for the next item.

QR / BARCODE SCANNER
• Open scanner from the stock-code field icon.
• Scan runs automatically on successful decode.
• Camera permission is required in browser settings.

stockTransfer.title: Stock Transfer
stockTransfer.subtitle: Transfer stock between locations for the same stock code
stockTransfer.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock Transfer moves a quantity of stock from one storage location to another for the same stock code. Two movements are posted simultaneously: a Transfer Out (type G) from the source location and a Transfer In (type C) to the destination location. The reference and user name are stamped on both movements for traceability.

HOW TO RECORD A STOCK TRANSFER

Step 1 — Find the stock
There are two ways to find the stock:
• Type the stock code in the input field and click Find Stock, or
• Click the search (magnifier) icon to open the product search — type a product name to find it, then select it to populate the stock code automatically.
• Alternatively, use the camera scanner icon to scan a barcode or QR code.

If the stock code is not found, a warning is shown and no movement can be recorded.

Step 2 — Select source and destination locations
The product name, stock code, and unit of measure are shown. A location table lists every storage location for that stock code with its current quantity and available quantity. The table has two checkbox columns: Out (source) and In (destination).
• Click Out on the row you want to transfer stock from.
• Click In on the row you want to transfer stock to.
• A location cannot be selected as both Out and In at the same time.
• To transfer to a location not yet in the list, use the New Location option at the bottom, or pick from extra system locations shown below existing rows.
  Note: If the system location limit is reached, you must choose an existing location.

Step 3 — Enter reference
Type a Reference (mandatory). This is recorded on both movements alongside your name. Examples: WT-2025-005, Bin Relocation.

Step 4 — Enter quantity
Enter the Transfer Quantity (must be greater than zero). The system validates that the quantity does not exceed the available stock at the source location.

Step 5 — Click Save
Both movements (Out and In) are saved together. The location table refreshes to show the updated quantities at both locations. A success message confirms the save. The reference and quantity fields clear for the next transaction.

QR / BARCODE SCANNER
• Click the scanner icon inside the stock code field to open the camera.
• Point the camera at a barcode or QR code — it scans automatically and the lookup runs immediately.
• The scanner closes after a successful scan.
• Camera access must be permitted in your browser settings.

stockIn.title: Stock In
stockIn.subtitle: Scan or enter stock code and record stock-in movements
stockIn.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock In records receipt into inventory (movement type I). It supports scan/find by stock code, product matching for unknown codes, optional product creation, location selection, reference entry, and quantity posting.

UPDATED FLOW
1. Scan or enter stock code
Use scanner icon or type stock code, then run Find Stock.

2. If stock is found
Product details and stock rows are shown.
• Select target stock row/location.
• Choose another existing location or create a new one when location limit allows.

3. If stock is NOT found
A product matching dialog with a list of products opens.
• User can select product from the product list to link a new stock code to a product.
• Optionally click on AI Product Search button to let AI find out what product the stock code is.
• Review candidate products and select one, then click Use Selected Product to link the stock code.
• If none is suitable, click No Product Matches to open Create New Product.

AI PRODUCT SEARCH (IMPORTANT)
• AI returns candidate products and may return a suggested name/description for prefill.
• AI does NOT create products and does NOT auto-link stock codes.
• Linking occurs only after explicit user action: Use Selected Product or Save Product And Continue.
• If AI matching fails or is unavailable, you can continue by manually selecting an existing product or creating a new one.

4. Create New Product path
Complete required fields (Product Code, Product Name, Category, UOM, and at least one image).
• Save Product And Continue: creates product, links stock code, and returns to stock-in flow.
• Back to Product Selection: returns to candidate list without creating product.

5. Enter reference and quantity
• Reference is mandatory for audit tracking.
• Stock In Quantity must be greater than zero.

6. Save and verify
Click Save to post movement. Quantities refresh and success message confirms completion.

QR / BARCODE SCANNER
• Open scanner from stock-code input icon.
• Successful decode triggers lookup automatically.
• Browser camera permission is required.

stockOut.title: Stock Out
stockOut.subtitle: Scan or enter stock code and record stock-out movements
stockOut.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock Out records the issue or dispatch of goods from a storage location. Each entry is saved as a stock-out movement (type O) against a specific stock code and location. The reference and current user name are stamped on every movement for traceability. You can only issue stock that already exists in the system — if a stock code is not found, no movement can be created.

HOW TO RECORD A STOCK OUT

Step 1 — Find the stock
There are two ways to find the stock:
• Type the stock code in the input field and click Find Stock, or
• Click the search (magnifier) icon to open the product search — type a product name to find it, then select it to populate the stock code automatically.
• Alternatively, use the camera scanner icon to scan a barcode or QR code.

If the stock code is not found in the system, a warning is shown and no movement can be recorded.

Step 2 — Select a location
The product name, stock code, and unit of measure are shown. A location table lists every storage location for that stock code with its current quantity and available quantity.
• Click a location row (or its checkbox) to select where to issue the stock from.
• Check the Available quantity — issuing more than the available quantity is not recommended as it may result in a negative balance.

Step 3 — Enter reference
Type a Reference (mandatory). This is recorded on the movement alongside your name. Examples: WO-2025-042, Issue Note 88.

Step 4 — Enter quantity
Enter the Stock Out Quantity (must be greater than zero).

Step 5 — Click Save
The stock-out movement is saved. The location table refreshes immediately to show the updated current and available quantities. A success message confirms the save. The reference field clears for the next transaction.

QR / BARCODE SCANNER
• Click the scanner icon inside the stock code field to open the camera.
• Point the camera at a barcode or QR code — it scans automatically and the lookup runs immediately.
• The scanner closes after a successful scan.
• Camera access must be permitted in your browser settings.

stockEnquiry.title: Stock Enquiry
stockEnquiry.subtitle: Enquire stock level by product, stock location, and movement
stockEnquiry.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Stock Enquiry is a read-only screen that displays current stock levels and the full movement history for all stock items. Data is loaded automatically when the page opens. Use the filters to narrow the results by stock code, product, location, reference, or movement type, and switch between Summary and Detail views to see the level of information you need.

PAGE LAYOUT

Filters panel
Five filter fields appear at the top of the screen:
• Stock Code — type part or all of a stock code to show only matching records.
• Product — type part of a product name to filter by product.
• Stock Location — type part of a location name to show only that location.
• Reference — type part of a reference value to find specific movements.
• Movement — select a movement type from the dropdown (e.g. Stock In, Stock Out, Take-On, Transfer). Select All to clear this filter.

All filters work instantly as you type — no need to click Enquire after changing a filter.

View Mode toggle
Use the Summary / Detail toggle to switch how the results are displayed.

Refresh button
Click the refresh icon to reload all stock data from the server.

SUMMARY VIEW
Summary view shows one row per stock code grouped by product. Each row contains:
• Stock Code — the unique identifier for the stock item.
• Product — the product name linked to the stock code.
• Location — the storage location for this stock line.
• Unit — unit of measure.
• Movements — total number of recorded movements for this stock line.
• Last Movement — date of the most recent movement.
• Baseline — the reference quantity from which movements are calculated.
• Current — the current stock balance (Baseline plus net stock movements).
• Available — the quantity available for use (Current plus held/reserved movements).

DETAIL VIEW
Detail view uses a hierarchical layout to show every individual movement:

1. Product header row (shown with a bold or highlighted background)
   Shows the product name and the total Current and Available quantities across all stock lines for that product.

2. Stock line total row (indented under the product)
   Shows the stock code and the cumulative totals for that stock line: net quantity moved, held quantity, Current, and Available.

3. Movement rows (indented under the stock line total)
   One row per individual movement, ordered from newest to oldest. Columns:
   • Date — when the movement was recorded.
   • Reference — the reference entered at the time of the transaction.
   • Location — storage location for this movement.
   • Movement — the movement type description (e.g. Stock In, Stock Out, Take-On, Transfer Out, Transfer In, In Adjustment, Out Adjustment).
   • Moved — the quantity that changed stock balance in this movement.
   • Held — the quantity that affected the hold/reserved balance.

FILTERED TOTALS NOTE
When one or more filters are active, all totals shown (Current, Available) reflect only the filtered rows, not the full stock position. Clear all filters to see the true overall stock balance.

COMMON TASKS

Check current stock for a product
Type the product name in the Product filter. Switch to Summary view to see each stock line with its current and available quantity.

View all movements for a stock code
Type the stock code in the Stock Code filter and switch to Detail view. All movements are listed in reverse chronological order under the stock line total row.

Find movements by reference number
Type all or part of the reference (e.g. a purchase order number or audit reference) in the Reference filter. Detail view will show the matching movement rows.

Filter by movement type
Open the Movement dropdown and select the type you need (e.g. Stock In to see all receipts, Stock Out to see all issues).

Reset all filters
Clear each filter field manually, or reload the page to return to the full unfiltered view.

Quick paste: double-click a product, stock code, location, or reference in the table or list to paste it into the matching filter.

receivePoStock.title: Receive PO Stock
receivePoStock.subtitle: Receive purchase-order stock into a location and record the receipt
receivePoStock.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Receive PO Stock receives goods against a purchase order and records the transaction as a Receive work order. The backend then creates stock-in movements and marks the PO as RECEIVED.

HOW TO USE
1. Select an eligible purchase order (status must be READY).
2. Choose the location to receive the stock into. You may select an existing location or type a new one.
3. For each PO line, scan or type the physical stock code(s) received and enter the quantity for each scan.
4. The received total per line is compared to the PO quantity.
5. If the totals differ, execution is blocked. You must either adjust the scanned quantities or amend the PO quantity after confirming with the vendor.
6. Click Execute Receipt to create the work order, run the receipt, refresh the PO, and generate a Goods Receipt Note PDF.

PDF
After a successful receipt, a PDF is generated and stored in the Stock Receipts document library. The file name includes the PO number and the latest PO status.

transferOut.title: Stock Dispatch
transferOut.subtitle: Dispatch inventory from a location to a remote warehouse
transferOut.helpBody:
OVERVIEW
Transfer Out records the movement of inventory out of a source location for delivery to a remote warehouse. The destination is taken from the selected Delivery Order project code, so only one location scan is required. The backend creates a Transferred Out movement (type G) and generates a Transfer Out Note PDF.

HOW TO USE
1. Select the Delivery Order being fulfilled.
2. Scan or select the source location the stock will leave from.
3. Scan or type each stock code being transferred. Only inventory/consumable products (category C) are allowed.
4. Adjust the transfer quantity for each scanned item if needed.
5. Capture at least one photo of the loaded stock for audit purposes.
6. Click Execute Transfer Out to create the work order and generate the PDF.

workOrder.subtitle: Manage and track work orders
workOrder.helpBody: Manage work orders: add, edit, and track work orders. Click a work order to view or edit details.

help.overview: The Work Order module manages operational tasks assigned to staff. A work order records what needs to be done, who does it, what materials or personnel are involved, and tracks progress through a defined lifecycle.
help.statusOpen: OPEN – Created and editable; awaiting preparation
help.statusIssued: ISSUED – Issued to staff for execution; visible on staff mobile portal
help.statusInProgress: INPROGRESS – Staff has started work; no further changes allowed
help.iconView: Eye (View) – Opens a read-only summary. Available for ISSUED and above.
help.iconEdit: Pencil (Edit) – Opens the edit form. Available for OPEN always; ISSUED only for Level 2+ users.
help.iconDetails: Grid (Details) – Opens detail items (products or staff). Red = not ready, Green = ready.
help.iconSteps: List (Steps) – Opens the steps form. Red = not ready, Green = ready.
help.iconIssue: Send (Issue) – Issues the work order. Appears only when all steps and details are complete.
help.createStep2: Select a Work Order Type. The type determines required steps and detail items.
help.createStep3: Fill in Description, Date, and Assigned To.
help.createStep4: Click Save. The new order is created with status OPEN.
help.stepsBody: Click the Steps icon. Fill in From and To for each step. Steps involving a worker entity are pre-filled from the assigned staff. The icon turns green when all required fields are filled.
help.detailsBody: Click the Details icon. Depending on the work order type's content type:
help.detailsStock: Stock – Select a Consumable product (category C) and enter quantity
help.detailsAsset: Asset – Select an Asset product (category A) and enter quantity
help.detailsWorker: Worker – Select a staff member (quantity is always 1)
help.detailsRules: Rules: No duplicate products or staff. Wrong product category is rejected.
help.issueBody: Click the Send icon when all steps and details are complete. Review the summary and click Issue Work Order. The status changes to ISSUED and the work order appears on the staff mobile portal.
help.issueNote: Once issued, only Level 2+ users can edit the work order.
help.viewBody: Click the Eye icon on any ISSUED or above work order to see a read-only summary including header, steps, and detail items.
